However, after much persuasion Bill Bird made our three in the 3000 metres team race, but not being at his best he finished well down. Ray Tooby ran well to be placed third (How about that Club Vest Ray?) and George Davidson was fifth.

A fast start saw a keen struggle for the lead with our second claim member, Bill Bird of Ranelagh actually leading during the early stages. Ken Norris and Peter Driver soon asserted themselves however, and pulled away from Ibbotson and Firth.
Jack's progress was a treat to watch, for from 6 miles he slowly went through to pass Keily, Hicks, Heywood, our second claim member Bill Bird, running a 'blinder', and was soon lying about 15th.

We were short of good milers in the Senior event, Herne Hill again taking maximum points, with Bill Bird 3rd. In the Junior 440 yds a new member, Venton, running in his first race for the Club was placed 4th, and in the Senior event Herne Hill again took maximum points with Glenn and Fox scoring 3rd and 4th for us.

A good field turned out for this race, including Bill Bird our second claim member, and of course Pete Newell the holder. From the start Bill took the field along at a very brisk pace and by the half distance only Pete Newell was still with him.

Walker had moved ahead and was some twenty places in front of Dabbs, with Bill Bird, second claim to Bels., just ahead. David had moved ahead of Eric who was losing a little ground, whilst Clive Shippen and Eddie Short had maintained their positions.
Bill Bird, as is his wont, was soon setting the pace with Bob Norton at his shoulder, and at 3 laps a group of eight had detached itself from the field.
He had his first serious dabble at 3 miling during this time, and in the L.C.C.Championships finished 3rd behind Pat Newell and Bill Bird in a best ever 14:30.2 - a time he is not proud of.
